title: Manipulating Strings
bullets: Clean, separate, modify, and convert string values.

title: Working with String Values
paragraphs: Strings store information as text.
Even when a string contains numbers, those values behave like text until they are converted to another data type.
Understanding common string methods makes it easier to clean, separate, modify, and convert data.

title: lower() / upper() / capitalize() / title()
paragraphs: These string methods change the capitalization of text.
lower() makes all letters lowercase, while upper() makes them uppercase
capitalize() capitalizes the first character, and title() capitalizes the first letter of each word.
These methods return a new string rather than changing the original string.
code:
text = "hello WORLD"

print(text.lower())
print(text.upper())
print(text.capitalize())
print(text.title())
initialOutput:
hello world
HELLO WORLD
Hello world
Hello World
expectedOutput:
hello world
HELLO WORLD
Hello world
Hello World

title: strip() / lstrip() / rstrip()
paragraphs: These methods remove whitespace from the beginning or end of a string.
strip() removes whitespace from both sides, while lstrip() removes it from the left and rstrip() removes it from the right.
They are especially useful when cleaning text.
terminalNote: In this example, the white space is highlighted in grey for emphasis.

title: split()
paragraphs: The split() method separates a string into a list of smaller strings.
Without a parameter, it normally splits the text wherever whitespace appears.
A separator can also be provided to split the string at a specific character or sequence.
code:
# No separator used
sentence = "red green blue"

print(sentence.split())

title: split()
paragraphs: The split() method separates a string into a list of smaller strings.
Without a parameter, it normally splits the text wherever whitespace appears.
A separator can also be provided to split the string at a specific character or sequence.
code:
# Uses , as a separator
data = "Alex,82,91"

print(data.split(","))

title: replace()
paragraphs: The replace() method creates a new string where one piece of text has been replaced with another.
It can replace individual characters, words, or longer sequences of text.
The original string is not changed unless the returned value is stored.

title: join()
paragraphs: The join() method combines multiple strings into one string.
It is called on the string that should be placed between each value.
This is useful for rebuilding text after it has been separated into a list.

title: Casting to int() or float()
paragraphs: Numbers stored inside strings cannot be used directly for normal mathematical operations.
int() converts a string into an integer, while float() converts it into a decimal number.
This is commonly necessary when numeric data is stored as text.
code:
age_text = "16"
price_text = "12.50"

age = int(age_text)
price = float(price_text)
